mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 YoY growth falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and a deceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a labor-intensive, low-investment growth regime, which historically precedes weaker earnings revisions and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when PAYEMS accelerates and INDPRO decelerates as specified.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic output, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -0.5% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during four consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) and Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a shift toward household investment and saving, which historically coincides with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to improved balance-sheet health and consumption expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both exceed 12-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six months in a low-inflation environment (CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%) signals an extended accommodative monetary policy stance, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for >6 months AND CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during episodes where FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for more than six months and inflation is below 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 4% signals robust aggregate demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 YoY growth exceeds 4%.
